data.narrative:
INTALUS is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Gene Skiba and Peter Ostlund that has raised $31M to date. The broader robotics and manufacturing sector includes one public comparable (277810.KQ) and eight private peers including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI, though none share INTALUS's precise stage and valuation profile in sufficient number for peer-median analysis.

Given data constraints, stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation approach. Using total raised ($31M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progressions yields an implied valuation of $78M. This method reflects standard venture progression patterns, though it relies on capital raised as a proxy given limited comparables.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $66M to $89M, with a median of $78M. Key uncertainties include the absence of a sufficiently dense peer set for cross-validation—only one same-stage comparable was identified in the robotics sector—and reliance on stage-based multiples rather than market-derived metrics. Revenue, unit economics, and technology differentiation data would materially sharpen this range. The $66M–$89M band should be treated as illustrative pending access to operational metrics or additional transaction data from the robotics manufacturing space.
